entities.name: Teimuraz I of Kakheti
entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Teimuraz I, of the Bagrationi dynasty, was a Georgian monarch (mepe) who ruled, with intermissions, as King of Kakheti from 1605 to 1648 and also of Kartli from 1629 to 1633. The eldest son of David I and Ketevan, Teimuraz spent most of his childhood at the court of Shah of Iran, where he came to be known as Tahmuras Khan. He was made king of Kakheti following a revolt against his reigning uncle, Constantine I, in 1605. From 1614 on, he waged a five-decade long struggle against the Safavid Iranian domination of Georgia in the course of which he lost several members of his family and ended his life as the Shah's prisoner at Astarabad at the age of 74.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Teimuraz I's five-decade long struggle against Safavid Iranian domination had significant regional impact on Georgia, resulting in the loss of several family members and ultimately ending his life as a prisoner. His reign marked a period of instability and power struggles within the Bagrationi dynasty.
